items.title: Recording and triaging a health observation
items.question: How should a suspected sick animal be assessed and recorded?
alternatives: how do I report a sick cow
items.answer: Observe safely, identify the animal, record objective signs and severity with the actual time and observer, and escalate urgent cases to the veterinarian. A DairyOS entry is evidence capture, not a diagnosis.
items.explanation: DairyOS Health stores an attributable observation record. It does not infer a diagnosis from the signs recorded, and it does not open a withdrawal period. Withdrawal arises only once a treatment carrying a withdrawal interval is recorded. Keeping observation, diagnosis and treatment as separate records is what makes the clinical history auditable and stops a suspicion hardening into a fact.

scenario.given: An operator notices a change in appetite, behaviour, respiration, gait, temperature, milk yield or general condition in fictional cow EX-COW-003.
steps: Protect people and animal welfare first.
Identify and separate the animal where farm protocol allows.
Record observed signs, measured values, the actual time and the observer in Health.
Assign severity from the governed vocabulary.
Notify the responsible supervisor or veterinarian for concerning signs.
scenario.expected: A dated, attributable observation exists, distinct from any diagnosis or treatment, and urgent care was not delayed by data entry.
scenario.next: The veterinarian determines examination, differential diagnosis, sampling, treatment and follow-up.

persisted: health observation with signs, measured values and time
projected: operational findings and alerts where thresholds are met

exceptions.condition: The animal cannot be safely approached.
exceptions.behaviour: Record the observation at distance and escalate. Do not force handling to complete a field.

exceptions.condition: The observation is recorded against the wrong animal.
exceptions.behaviour: Follow correction_path. DairyOS preserves history rather than deleting it.

exceptions.condition: Signs suggest a contagious or herd-level problem.
exceptions.behaviour: Escalate immediately rather than completing data entry first.

items.correction_path: Record a corrected observation against the right animal and annotate the erroneous record. DairyOS preserves history rather than removing it.
items.safety: Do not diagnose, prescribe, or delay emergency veterinary care based on Assistant guidance.

perspectives.operator: Record what you can see and measure. Escalate anything concerning rather than waiting.
perspectives.supervisor: Check that observations carry an observer and a real time, and that escalation actually happened.
perspectives.veterinary_health: The record is evidence for examination, not a diagnosis, and it does not itself restrict milk.
perspectives.technical: Written through the Health API and propagated to passport history by health_management_service.
perspectives.training: Practise on a fictional animal such as EX-COW-003.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If the observation is missing from passport history, confirm the animal identity used at entry.

items.title: Assigning health severity
items.question: How should health severity be recorded?
items.answer: Use objective signs and the approved severity vocabulary. Severity supports triage and prioritisation; it does not establish a diagnosis.
items.explanation: Severity is a triage signal that makes urgency visible to whoever reviews the case next. It is deliberately separate from diagnosis: a severe classification says the animal needs attention soon, not what is wrong with it. Because alerts and findings are driven from severity, a habitually understated severity quietly suppresses the very alerts meant to protect the animal.

scenario.given: A new health observation is being entered for fictional cow EX-COW-003.
steps: Record the objective signs first.
Select the supported severity level.
Escalate urgent signs immediately rather than relying on the alert.
Save and verify the case history.
scenario.expected: Urgency is visible without any clinical diagnosis having been invented.
scenario.next: Record veterinarian-authorised treatment and follow-up separately.

exceptions.condition: Signs are ambiguous.
exceptions.behaviour: Record the signs and choose severity conservatively. Escalate rather than downgrade.

exceptions.condition: Severity was assigned incorrectly.
exceptions.behaviour: Record a corrected observation. The original classification remains in history.

items.correction_path: Record a corrected observation carrying the right severity. The superseded classification stays auditable.
items.safety: Severity is not a diagnosis, and a low severity never justifies delaying veterinary attention when signs are concerning.

perspectives.operator: Pick the level that matches what you saw, and escalate urgent cases directly rather than waiting for an alert.
perspectives.supervisor: Watch for systematic under-grading; it suppresses the alerts the farm relies on.
perspectives.veterinary_health: Severity communicates urgency for triage, not a clinical grade.
perspectives.technical: Severity drives alert and finding generation from the recorded case.
perspectives.training: Grade a set of fictional observations and compare reasoning.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If expected alerts do not appear, check the severity recorded on the case.

items.title: Recording a veterinary treatment
items.question: What must be recorded when a veterinarian treats an animal?
items.answer: Record the animal, the treatment or product, the actual date and time, the responsible person, the clinical context, and the veterinarian-authorised instructions including any withdrawal interval. Clinical diagnosis and prescription authority remain with the veterinarian.
items.explanation: A treatment is the event that can restrict milk, so it carries the withdrawal instruction. DairyOS does not hold a table of withdrawal periods and does not calculate one: the interval comes from the product label or the veterinarian and is entered with the treatment. DairyOS then stores that interval and enforces it. This is why a treatment recorded without its withdrawal instruction leaves a food-safety gap that no downstream check can close.

scenario.given: A veterinarian has authorised and administered a treatment to fictional cow EX-COW-003.
steps: Confirm animal identity and treatment authority.
Record the product or treatment and the administration details.
Record the veterinarian or responsible professional.
Enter the milk and meat withdrawal instruction from the product label or the veterinarian.
Verify the animal's active withdrawal state and follow-up date.
scenario.expected: The treatment is traceable, attributable, and food-safety controls can identify the affected milk.
scenario.next: Do not send affected milk to sale. Use the governed withdrawal and disposition workflow.

persisted: treatment event with product, date and administering party
derived: active withdrawal state for the animal

exceptions.condition: The product carries no withdrawal period.
exceptions.behaviour: Record that explicitly. Do not leave the field empty and assume none applies.

exceptions.condition: The withdrawal instruction is not known at the time of recording.
exceptions.behaviour: Obtain it from the label or the veterinarian before milk is dispositioned. Do not guess a value.

exceptions.condition: The treatment is amended or discontinued.
exceptions.behaviour: Record the change as a further event. The original treatment fact is retained.

items.correction_path: Record a corrective or amending treatment event. The original entry is never erased, because withdrawal decisions may already have been taken against it.
items.safety: DairyOS must not invent drug doses, routes, durations or withdrawal periods, and neither may the Assistant. Those values come from the product label and the veterinarian.

perspectives.operator: Enter the treatment with the withdrawal instruction you were given; never estimate it.
perspectives.supervisor: A treatment recorded without its withdrawal instruction is a food-safety gap, not a tidy-up task.
perspectives.finance: Milk withheld for withdrawal is excluded from sold litres and therefore from revenue.
perspectives.veterinary_health: Diagnosis and prescription authority stay with the veterinarian; DairyOS records the authorised instruction.
perspectives.technical: WithdrawalPeriod stores explicit start_time and end_time; no withdrawal duration is held or computed in code.
perspectives.training: Practise with a fictional product and a fictional interval supplied in the exercise.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If an animal does not show as withdrawn, check that the treatment carried a withdrawal interval at all.

items.title: How withdrawal keeps treated milk out of sale
items.question: What is a withdrawal period, and how does DairyOS keep milk from a treated animal out of sales?
alternatives: when can I sell her milk again
items.answer: A withdrawal period is the interval after a treatment during which the animal's milk must not enter the sale stream. DairyOS stores the interval recorded with the treatment and uses it to identify affected animals, so the milk can be handled as non-sale until the period ends.
items.explanation: DairyOS holds a withdrawal as an explicit start time and end time attached to a treatment. It does not derive the length from the product, because no table of withdrawal periods exists in the software; the interval is whatever was entered from the label or veterinary direction. The check is half-open, meaning the animal counts as withdrawn from the start time up to but not including the end time, so it is clear on the end time rather than after it. Affected milk is recorded as a non-sale disposition with its reason, which is what keeps it traceable and out of sold litres and revenue.

scenario.given: Fictional cow EX-COW-003 has an active milk withdrawal recorded against a treatment.
steps: Check the animal and the withdrawal end date and time.
Keep the milk out of the sale stream.
Record the resulting non-sale disposition with its reason.
Verify the health summary and the milk reconciliation reflect the withheld volume.
scenario.expected: Affected milk is traceable, excluded from sold litres and revenue, and the withheld volume reconciles.
scenario.next: Recheck the animal after the withdrawal end time. Treatment history is retained regardless.

persisted: withdrawal interval attached to the treatment
derived: whether the animal is withdrawn at a given time

exceptions.condition: The milk looks and tests normal during the withdrawal.
exceptions.behaviour: It remains withheld. Appearance is not evidence that residue has cleared.

exceptions.condition: The check falls exactly on the withdrawal end time.
exceptions.behaviour: The animal is no longer withdrawn, because the interval is end-exclusive.

exceptions.condition: An animal has more than one active withdrawal.
exceptions.behaviour: The animal is withdrawn while any one of them is active.

items.correction_path: Correct the underlying treatment record. A withdrawal is never shortened directly, because it exists only as a property of the treatment that created it.
items.safety: Never override or shorten a withdrawal period because the milk appears normal. Confirm with the veterinarian or the product authority. The Assistant cannot supply a withdrawal length for any product and will not estimate one.

perspectives.operator: While she is withdrawn, her milk does not go to the tank. Record where it went instead.
perspectives.supervisor: Check that withheld volume is dispositioned and reconciles, not simply omitted.
perspectives.finance: Withheld milk is excluded from sold litres and from revenue, and still counts as produced.
perspectives.veterinary_health: The interval comes from the product label or veterinary direction; DairyOS only enforces what was recorded.
perspectives.technical: WithdrawalPeriod.is_withdrawn evaluates start <= check < end, so the interval is end-exclusive.
perspectives.training: Given a fictional treatment time and a fictional interval, work out when milk may be sold again.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If milk was sold during a withdrawal, check whether the treatment carried an interval when it was recorded.

items.title: Following up an open health case
items.question: When should a health case be followed up?
items.answer: Follow-up is due according to the recorded clinical plan. Review at the due date, record the outcome and any changed plan, and keep the case open while clinical work remains.
items.explanation: Follow-up exists so that open clinical work stays visible rather than being assumed complete. Recording a treatment does not close a case, and neither does acknowledging an alert. The follow-up record is the evidence that someone actually looked again, which is what separates a case that improved from one that was simply forgotten.

scenario.given: Fictional cow EX-COW-003 has a treatment with a follow-up requirement.
steps: Review the due date and the responsible person.
Re-examine, or obtain the required veterinary result.
Record the outcome and any changed plan.
Keep the case open if clinical work remains.
scenario.expected: Open clinical work stays visible until it is genuinely complete.
scenario.next: Resolve the case when the defined outcome is met, or escalate if signs persist or worsen.

derived: case remains open or becomes resolvable
projected: alerts and findings for overdue follow-up

exceptions.condition: The follow-up is overdue.
exceptions.behaviour: The case stays open and continues to surface. An overdue prompt is not closed by acknowledging it.

exceptions.condition: A distinct new problem appears at follow-up.
exceptions.behaviour: Create a new case rather than extending the existing one.

items.correction_path: Record a further follow-up observation. Earlier follow-up records are retained.
items.safety: Escalate if signs persist or worsen rather than waiting for the next scheduled follow-up.

perspectives.operator: Look again at the due date and write down what you found, even when nothing changed.
perspectives.supervisor: Overdue follow-ups are the clearest early signal that case management is slipping.
perspectives.veterinary_health: Follow-up evidence is clinical, and its absence means the outcome is unknown rather than good.
perspectives.technical: health_management_service holds the case lifecycle; health_action_service drives follow-up prompts.
perspectives.training: Work a fictional case from observation through follow-up.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If a case will not resolve, check whether the required follow-up evidence has actually been recorded.

items.title: Closing a health case
items.question: How should a health case be closed?
items.answer: A case is resolved only after the authorised follow-up evidence is recorded. Acknowledging an alert or entering a treatment does not by itself prove recovery.
items.explanation: Resolution is a claim that the underlying problem is finished, so DairyOS requires the evidence that supports it rather than a status change alone. The lifecycle from observation through severity, treatment, withdrawal and follow-up stays auditable after resolution, so a resolved case can still be examined. A resolved status is a record of someone's judgement, not a clinical fact in itself.

scenario.given: Fictional cow EX-COW-003 has a treated case whose follow-up has been recorded and the animal has recovered.
steps: Open the existing case and confirm its history.
Confirm the defined outcome has been met.
Record the resolving evidence and the responsible person.
Resolve the case.
scenario.expected: The lifecycle from observation through treatment and resolution remains auditable after closure.
scenario.next: Continue routine monitoring, and create a new case if a distinct problem occurs.

persisted: resolution with its evidence and responsible person
derived: case no longer counted as open

exceptions.condition: An active withdrawal is still running.
exceptions.behaviour: Resolving the case does not end the withdrawal. The withdrawal is a property of the treatment and runs to its end time.

exceptions.condition: Signs return after resolution.
exceptions.behaviour: Create a new case. Do not reopen history to absorb a fresh problem.

items.correction_path: Record a further observation or a new case. A resolution already recorded stays in history.
items.safety: A resolved status is not a substitute for clinical evidence, and resolving a case never shortens a withdrawal period.

perspectives.operator: Close it when she is actually better and you have written down how you know.
perspectives.supervisor: Cases closed without follow-up evidence are the ones worth auditing.
perspectives.veterinary_health: Resolution records a judgement of completion, not a verified cure.
perspectives.technical: Case lifecycle state is held by health_management_service; withdrawal state is independent of it.
perspectives.training: Close a fictional case, then check that the withdrawal is unaffected.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If milk is still restricted after resolution, that is correct: check the treatment's withdrawal end time.

items.authoring_note: NEW ITEM. The catalogue lists capability 'resolution' under health-and-veterinary, but the only item carrying that capability was dashboard.resolution, a Dashboard item. The validator's capability coverage check is domain-blind, so this gap was masked. Content is split out from the previous combined health.follow-up-resolution authoring.

items.title: What the health summary shows
items.question: What does the health summary represent?
alternatives: where do I see health status
items.answer: It is a projection of recorded health observations, treatments, withdrawals, vaccinations and follow-up status. It is not an independent diagnosis and it is not a separate source of truth.
items.explanation: The summary is derived from the underlying clinical records, so it can only be as complete as they are. When a summary count disagrees with the source histories, the source histories are authoritative and the discrepancy points to a recording problem rather than a display problem. This is why the summary is never edited directly.

steps: Check the summary date and the population it covers.
Open material cases and active withdrawals.
Compare summary counts against the source histories.
Escalate discrepancies rather than editing the summary.
scenario.expected: The summary supports management decisions while the source clinical facts remain authoritative.
scenario.next: Use the Health workflow for corrections or new observations.

audit: traceable to the underlying case, treatment and vaccination records

exceptions.condition: A summary count disagrees with the source history.
exceptions.behaviour: The source history is authoritative. Investigate the recording, do not adjust the summary.

exceptions.condition: The summary appears empty.
exceptions.behaviour: Confirm the date and population selected before concluding there are no cases.

items.correction_path: Correct the underlying clinical record through the Health workflow. The summary recomputes from it.
items.safety: The summary is a management view, not a clinical assessment, and an empty summary is not evidence of a healthy herd.

perspectives.operator: Use it to see what needs attention, then open the actual case.
perspectives.supervisor: Compare counts against source histories periodically; divergence indicates recording gaps.
perspectives.finance: Active withdrawals indicate milk that will not reach sale.
perspectives.veterinary_health: It aggregates records; it makes no clinical judgement.
perspectives.technical: Served by GET /farm/health/summary and rendered on HealthTab and the dashboard.
perspectives.training: Trace one fictional summary count back to the records that produced it.
perspectives.troubleshooting: A count that looks wrong is almost always a missing or misattributed source record.

items.title: Recording a vaccination
items.question: What must be recorded after a vaccine is given?
items.answer: Record the animal or group, the actual administered date, the vaccine or product, the batch or lot where available, the administrator or veterinarian, the next due date, the route or site where the approved programme requires it, and any reaction or note.
items.explanation: Vaccination is a separate DairyOS capability from general Health, and a vaccination event is a preventive record rather than a treatment or a health case. Keeping them distinct matters: a vaccination does not open a health case, does not imply illness, and does not by itself create a withdrawal. The next due date recorded on the event is what drives due and overdue tracking.

scenario.given: An authorised vaccination has been completed on fictional cow EX-COW-004.
steps: Confirm identity and eligibility.
Enter the actual administration date.
Capture product, batch and responsible person details.
Record the next due date.
Save and verify the event in the animal history or vaccination view.
scenario.expected: The event is an auditable preventive record and is not confused with a treatment or a health case.
scenario.next: Schedule the follow-up or booster according to the approved programme.

persisted: vaccination event with product, batch, date and administrator

exceptions.condition: The batch or lot is not available.
exceptions.behaviour: Record the event with what is known. Batch traceability is reduced but the event is still a fact.

exceptions.condition: The product carries a withdrawal instruction.
exceptions.behaviour: That instruction is recorded through the treatment and withdrawal workflow, not inferred from the vaccination event.

items.correction_path: Record a corrected event. Do not delete a vaccination record, since coverage history depends on it.
items.safety: The Assistant will not supply a vaccine schedule, interval or dose. Those come from the veterinarian's region- and risk-specific programme and the product label.

perspectives.operator: Record it the day it is given, with the batch if you have it, and set the next due date.
perspectives.supervisor: Coverage is only as good as the next-due dates recorded on the events.
perspectives.finance: Vaccine purchases are recorded in Finance; the administration is a health record.
perspectives.veterinary_health: A vaccination is preventive and does not indicate illness.
perspectives.technical: Vaccination is a separate surface from Health cases, split deliberately.
perspectives.training: Record a fictional vaccination and observe where the next due date appears.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If an animal shows as overdue, check the next due date on the most recent event.

items.title: Designing a herd vaccination programme
items.question: How should a herd vaccination programme be designed?
alternatives: what vaccines does my herd need
items.answer: Start from the veterinarian's region- and risk-specific programme. Define target groups, product authority, timing, handling, boosters, exclusions, adverse-reaction escalation and coverage review before recording any administration.
items.explanation: DairyOS holds the programme as an approved plan and the administrations as attributable historical facts, and keeps the two apart. A plan is not evidence that anything was given, and a recorded event is not evidence that the plan was correct. There is no universal schedule: what a herd needs depends on disease prevalence, movement, product authorisation in the jurisdiction and veterinary judgement, so the programme is an input to DairyOS rather than an output from it.

scenario.given: A manager wants to improve herd protection on a fictional farm.
steps: Review disease history, herd classes, movement and reproductive risk with the veterinarian.
Define the approved schedule and the eligible population.
Record each completed event with product, date, animal or group, administrator and next due date.
Review overdue and missed animals.
scenario.expected: The programme remains an approved plan while actual administrations remain attributable historical facts.
scenario.next: Investigate missed or adverse events with the veterinarian.

persisted: vaccination events as they are completed

exceptions.condition: An animal is excluded from the programme.
exceptions.behaviour: The exclusion is part of the approved plan and should be recorded, not left as a silent gap.

exceptions.condition: Product authorisation differs by jurisdiction.
exceptions.behaviour: The programme follows local authorisation and the veterinarian's direction.

items.correction_path: Revise the approved programme with the veterinarian. Historical administrations are never altered to match a revised plan.
items.safety: DairyOS must not prescribe a universal vaccine schedule and must not replace veterinary or public-health authority. The Assistant explains how the capability works and will not design a programme for a herd.

perspectives.operator: Follow the programme your veterinarian set, and record every administration.
perspectives.supervisor: Review coverage and overdue animals rather than assuming the plan was executed.
perspectives.finance: Vaccine purchase costs are recorded in Finance as expenses.
perspectives.veterinary_health: The programme is region- and risk-specific and belongs to the veterinarian.
perspectives.technical: Coverage is derived from recorded events against the intended population.
perspectives.training: Discuss why a schedule appropriate on one farm may be wrong on another.
perspectives.troubleshooting: Poor coverage is usually unrecorded administrations rather than missed ones.

items.title: Missed vaccinations and adverse reactions
items.question: What should happen when a vaccination is missed or a reaction occurs?
items.answer: Do not invent a replacement date and do not repeat a dose on the strength of software advice. Record the operational concern, preserve the facts already known, obtain veterinary direction, and record the resulting action and follow-up.
items.explanation: A due reminder is a projection from the last recorded next-due date; it is not evidence that anything happened or failed to happen. Recording a vaccination that was not given in order to clear an overdue flag destroys the coverage record it was meant to protect. An adverse reaction is a clinical observation and is recorded through the Health workflow, which keeps the reaction linked to the animal without turning the vaccination event into a health case.

scenario.given: A due vaccination is missed, or fictional cow EX-COW-004 reacts after administration.
steps: Identify the animal or the affected cohort.
Record an observation or a follow-up need with the actual date and facts.
Escalate promptly to the veterinarian for the next action.
Record the authorised outcome and the next due date.
scenario.expected: An evidence trail is retained and no reminder has been turned into a completed vaccination.
scenario.next: Review programme coverage and any adverse-event pattern.

persisted: authorised outcome and revised next due date
audit: vaccination and health history kept distinct but linked

exceptions.condition: The vaccination was given but not recorded.
exceptions.behaviour: Record the actual event with its real date. This is a recording correction, not a new administration.

exceptions.condition: Several animals react.
exceptions.behaviour: Escalate as a cohort concern immediately rather than recording individually and waiting.

items.correction_path: Record the actual facts and the veterinarian-authorised outcome. Never backdate a vaccination that did not occur.
items.safety: The Assistant will not advise repeating a dose, choosing a replacement date, or managing a reaction. Those require veterinary direction, and a severe reaction is an emergency.

perspectives.operator: If it was missed, say so. Do not enter a date to make the flag go away.
perspectives.supervisor: An overdue flag clearing without a matching administration is a warning sign.
perspectives.veterinary_health: Reactions are clinical events and are recorded as health observations.
perspectives.technical: Reaction records live in the Health case surface; vaccination events remain in the vaccination surface.
perspectives.training: Work through a fictional missed dose and a fictional reaction.
perspectives.troubleshooting: If coverage looks better than reality, check for vaccinations recorded to clear overdue flags.
